Model family:
The Emax table shows three ranges: 45 kg up to 340 kg, 340 kg up to and including 1500 kg, 1500 kg up to and including 7500 kg. This corresponds to three model groups. Also the load cell transmission type: Bending beam vs Shear beam — with different Emax ranges per transmission type.

Looking at the table structure:
- Row: "Load cell transmission type" | (colspan=2) Bending beam | Shear beam
- Row: "Maximum capacity (Emax)" | 45 kg up to 340 kg | 340 kg up to and including 1500 kg | 1500 kg up to and including 7500 kg

So bending beam covers 45–340 kg and 340–1500 kg? Actually the colspan=2 for bending beam means bending beam applies to first two columns of Emax ranges, shear beam applies to... hmm wait. The Emax row has 3 columns: 45 kg up to 340 kg | 340 up to 1500 | 1500 up to 7500. The transmission type row has bending beam spanning 2 columns and shear beam 1 column. So bending beam: 45 kg to 1500 kg; shear beam: 1500 kg to 7500 kg.

Other rows vary across the three columns:
- Max number of load cell intervals (n): 3000, 3000, 3000 — same
- Y = Emax/Vmin: 14000, 11100, 11100 — varies
- Z = Emax/(2*DR): 3400, 5700, 5170 — varies

So there are three capacity classes. Model level entries:
- maximum_capacity ranges: {min: 45, max: 340} kg; {min: 340, max: 1500} kg; {min: 1500, max: 7500} kg
- max_load_cell_intervals_nlc: 3000 for all three (could be type level since same, but it varies per column structure... value is the same, but with footnote 1). I could put it in model_level with same values, or type level. Since it's the same across all, type_level is fine. But footnote marker 1 applies. Hmm, the schema has footnote_markers per value. Let me put n as model_level to keep structure parallel? Actually rule 4 says varying attributes in model_level. n is not varying (3000 in all three). I could put it in type_level with footnote_markers ["1)"]. That seems reasonable.

Actually, let me think about model IDs. I'll define models by capacity range and transmission type:
- "Bending beam, Emax 45–340 kg"
- "Bending beam, Emax 340–1500 kg"
- "Shear beam, Emax 1500–7500 kg"

Hmm, but wait — does bending beam apply to both first two columns? The colspan=2 suggests yes. Let me define model IDs:
- "CGSB (bending beam) Emax 45-340 kg" — but the type names include CGSB, CGSB-1, CGSB-SS, CGSB-SS-1. Possibly -SS = stainless steel (shear beam?). Actually "Transducer material: Alloy steel / Stainless steel". The type designations: CGSB (alloy steel bending beam?), CGSB-SS (stainless steel?). Not fully clear. Better not to over-infer.

I'll use model IDs based on capacity ranges:
- "Emax 45-340 kg (bending beam)"
- "Emax 340-1500 kg (bending beam)"
- "Emax 1500-7500 kg (shear beam)"

Model-level characteristics:
- maximum_capacity: ranges per model
- ratio_y_emax_over_vmin: 14000, 11100, 11100 (footnote 1)
- ratio_z_emax_over_dr: 3400, 5700, 5170 (footnote 1)
- max_load_cell_intervals_nlc: 3000 for all (footnote 1)

Type-level characteristics:
- loading_direction: "Compression or tension"
- accuracy_class: "C"
- rated_output: 3 mV/V ± 0.25% — value 3, unit "mV/V", tolerance? Could record as value 3, unit_symbol "mV/V", plus maybe rated_output_tolerance. I'll do value: 3, unit_symbol: "mV/V" and maybe a note. The ±0.25% is a tolerance. I could add "rated_output_tolerance": 0.25%. Keep it simple: value 3, unit mV/V.
- minimum_dead_load: 0 kg
- input_impedance: 385 Ω ± 10 Ω → value 385, unit "Ω", tolerance 10. Maybe record impedance_tolerance separately. I'll include input_impedance_tolerance: 10 Ω. Hmm, could be noisy. The schema says value can be number, range, or string. "385 Ω ± 10 Ω" — I could do value: 385, unit_symbol: "Ω". And add tolerance characteristics. I'll add them as separate ones: input_impedance_tolerance {value: 10, unit_symbol: "Ω"}, output_impedance_tolerance {value: 3, unit_symbol: "Ω"}.
- temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C"
- fraction_plc (apportionment_factor_plc): 0.7 (converted from 0,7)
- humidity_class: "CH"
- safe_overload: 150 % of Emax → value 150, unit "%", plus safe_overload_reference: "Emax"
- output_impedance: 350 Ω ± 3 Ω
- recommended_excitation: 10 V AC/DC → value 10, unit "V", and excitation type AC/DC. Maybe recommended_excitation_type: "AC / DC". 
- excitation_maximum: 20 V AC/DC
- transducer_material: "Alloy steel / Stainless steel"
- atmospheric_protection: "Silicone / RTV"
- load_cell_transmission_type: could be config/model level: bending beam for first two, shear beam for third. I'll put in model_level: attribute "load_cell_transmission_type", values per model.

- id: R60

- scheme: A
- accuracy_classes: ["C"]

- NMi-2452739-04, 13 October 2021, 24 pages, type_evaluation_report

Matrix tables: The characteristics table could be preserved as a matrix_table too. It's a capacity-class × attribute table. I think I can include it as a matrix table with columns and rows, or rely on model_level. The schema says matrix_tables preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere. Here the table does fit into model_level. But the transmission type dimension adds complexity — it's a 2-D structure (capacity range × transmission type mapped). I could include one matrix_table "Characteristics of the load cell" with columns: emax_range, transmission_type, max_load_cell_intervals_nlc, ratio_y_emax_over_vmin, ratio_z_emax_over_dr. Rows for the three classes. That preserves fidelity. I'll include it, plus model_level entries.

Units: kg for Emax ranges. Y and Z are dimensionless (null unit). n is dimensionless.

Footnote markers on values: n (1), Y (1), Z (1) → footnote_markers: ["1)"].

Decimal conversion: "3 mV/V ± 0,25%" → 0.25 tolerance. pLC 0,7 → 0.7.

Date format: I'll use ISO "2021-10-14". Test report dates "2021-10-13".

Now let me construct model IDs. Perhaps simpler: "CGSB-45-340", hmm. Let me use descriptive:
- "Emax=45-340kg (bending beam)"
- "Emax=340-1500kg (bending beam)"
- "Emax=1500-7500kg (shear beam)"

Model_level attributes:
1. maximum_capacity — hmm, it's a range per model. value: {min, max}, unit_symbol "kg".
2. load_cell_transmission_type — string values.
3. max_load_cell_intervals_nlc — 3000 each, footnote ["1)"]. Since same across models, could go type_level. But it's presented per column. I'll keep it in model_level for consistency with footnote handling... Actually rule: varying → model_level; constant could be type_level. n is constant at 3000. I'll put it in type_level with footnote_markers. Hmm but the schema for type_level value objects include footnote_markers — yes: `<label>: {value, unit, footnote_markers[]}`. OK, type_level: max_load_cell_intervals_nlc: {value: 3000, unit_symbol: null, footnote_markers: ["1)"]}.

Wait, the schema sketch shows type_level entries as {value, unit, footnote_markers[]}, but rule 3 requires value objects with value/unit_symbol/unit_id/footnote_markers. I'll use the rule-3 structured form consistently: {"value": ..., "unit_symbol": ..., "unit_id": null, "footnote_markers": [...]}.
